target.title: fix(synology-chat): evict stale chat user cache entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `chatUserCache` Map has a TTL of 5 minutes but only checks it on read — stale entries are never removed from the Map on write. A caller that rotates through many webhook URLs can therefore grow the Map without bound, leaking memory for the lifetime of the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding a cache eviction pass before each insert is a zero-risk fix: stale entries would not be returned by the read path anyway (`Date.now() - cached.cachedAt < CACHE_TTL_MS` check), so eviction merely reclaims memory they occupy. The only observable effect is that a subsequent read may re-fetch from the API, which is identical to the behavior when no cache entry exists.

## User Impact

Users with many Synology Chat webhook URLs (or a hostile caller) can no longer grow the chat user cache without bound.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` — passed
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/synology-chat/src/client.ts` — passed
- Mutation check: temporarily removing the eviction loop lets the Map grow unbounded; with the fix, each insert clears stale entries first.
- No behavior change for normal use (single or few webhook URLs).
